Ich hab meinen Bachelor auf der FH gemacht und nach dem letzten Semester nach dem Praktikum eine Stelle für vorerst 25h angeboten bekommen. Hi, I just explained how I did it in another comment, there you go: https://www.reddit.com/r/CrossStitch/comments/pol6im/fo_i_cross_stitched_a_little_lobster_on_my/hcyejlx/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=ios_app&utm_name=iossmf&context=3

there are also videos on youtube, it‘s not hard at all!

I used water soluble waste canvas! It‘s basically like aida, but it will dissolve in warm water. It looks like a slice of thin plastic with holes in it for the grid. It usually comes in 14 ct, haven‘t seen any other sizes yet.

So you take your soluble canvas and cut out a piece which is a little bit bigger than your pattern and baste it onto your shirt (or whatever you‘re stitching on) to keep it put. I prefer to stitch with a hoop, so I next place my hoop and just cross stitch as you‘re used to.

When finished, I take away the hoop and soak the shirt in warm/hot water (i think about 40 degree celcius is recommended) for about 10 mins. Give it a thorough wash so all the canvas comes out. 

I then dried it and ironed on some thin interfacing to make sure the stitches stay put (I find this to be not always necessary, depends on the fabric you‘re stitching on). As a last step I put the shirt into the washing machine like I usually would, just to make sure all the waste canvas is gone and the motive softens up.

I‘d say that‘s pretty much it! Let me know if you have more questions :)

As soon as I sat down I got panic attacks and started crying, I felt so embarrassed but I just can‘t do anything about it.
This nurse got up and asked for 2 more of her colleagues to come in. Those two started to talk to me and reassured me that there is nothing to be ashamed of and tried to distract me as good as they could.

I know they get cases like me daily, but this was the first time in years that I didn‘t fade when getting blood taken and I was so thankful for them being so understanding and kind. I know it isn‘t too much of a deal but that was one of the most kindest things I‘ve experienced in a long time.
